name: IgG4-Related Sclerosing Cholangitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Comprehensive Diagnostic Criteria for IgG4-Related Sclerosing Cholangitis

criteria.description: Characteristic bile duct imaging findings showing segmental or diffuse strictures with wall thickening
Histopathological evidence of dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration rich in IgG4-positive plasma cells and storiform fibrosis
Clinical and radiological improvement after corticosteroid therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic bile duct imaging findings plus elevated serum IgG4 and/or histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of malignancy and other causes of sclerosing cholangitis

pathognomonic.notes: Due to bile duct strictures causing cholestasis

rare.notes: Rarely reported in systemic IgG4-related disease

laboratory: Mild to moderate elevation of liver function tests (alkaline phosphatase, gamma-GT, bilirubin)
imaging: Cholangiography showing segmental or diffuse bile duct strictures with wall thickening
MRI/MRCP demonstrating bile duct irregularities and pancreatic involvement
CT scan showing bile duct wall thickening and possible pancreatic enlargement
other: Histopathology showing lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with IgG4-positive plasma cells and storiform fibrosis
Good clinical response to corticosteroid therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive clinical course without steroid response
Due to infections, ischemia, or toxins
History of biliary injury or infection

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss with mass lesion on imaging
Poor response or worsening despite corticosteroid therapy
references: Kamisawa T, et al. IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis: clinical features and diagnosis. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2010;17(5): 539-545.
Zen Y, Nakanuma Y. IgG4-related disease: a cross-sectional study of 114 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2010;34(12):1812-1819.
Chari ST, et al. Diagnosis of IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis. Gut. 2012;61(3): 408-414.
